chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Ammar al-Sabati said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who has a young wife, and she menstruates once every two or three months. How should her husband divorce her? He said: 'The matter of this is difficult; she is to be divorced with a single sunnah divorce, one pronouncement, during a period of purity from non-consummation, with witnesses. Then she is left alone until she menstruates three times. Whenever she has completed her three menstruations, her waiting period is concluded.'
I said to him: 'And if a year passes and she does not menstruate three times in it?' He said: 'He waits for her for three months after the year, then her waiting period is concluded.'
I said: 'And if she dies or her husband dies?' He said: 'Whichever of them dies, the survivor inherits from the other for the period between them and fifteen months.'

key_terms.طَلَاقُ السُّنَّةِ: Sunnah divorce (divorce in accordance with prophetic tradition)
key_terms.عِدَّةُ: Waiting period (iddah) after divorce or death
key_terms.وَرِثَهُ صَاحِبُهُ: The survivor inherits from the deceased

ai.seo_question: How is the waiting period (iddah) calculated for a woman with irregular menstruation who does not menstruate regularly?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the fiqh of *al-mustahaddah* (woman with irregular menstruation), establishing a dual mechanism for determining the *iddah* (waiting period) based on actual cycles or a fixed temporal duration. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing biological reality with legal certainty, ensuring the woman is neither prematurely released nor indefinitely bound. The ruling on inheritance for up to fifteen months further underscores the continuity of marital rights during this extended period of uncertainty.
